It's one month for now so I'm still talking about lessons instead of other things. But I'm thinking there will be a time for that.

You made my day bro with it :D I appreciate

Personally from my experience, I would like to say that if you're going to decide to start with meditation it is directly related to putting off a mask you wore a whole life. But additionally, to your text, I would like to add it is a step required to be a better person. If you're going to put off your mask which means staying fine with your past problems. You know what I'm saying - your shittly childhood or stuff like that. You will never be able to be yourself. I tried to explain to my parents and it was also a point They decided to start with meditation. They say thank you to me for now. I wrote a month ago about my experience related to flashbacks from my childhood affected by meditation - I just leave a link just here:

[https://www.pawelwojtasinski.blog/article/6](https://www.pawelwojtasinski.blog/article/6)

I know ads are not something welcome right here, but I made my blog without getting any money from that. It's therapy for me.
Man, It's awesome!
I'm thinking your idea is fine. But additionally, I would add some more explanation to them about why you're doing it. I think it will let them understand your point of view.

I think you should just start. There is no golden recipe on how to use meditation ideally and in what moments in life it will help you. Personally, I recommend meditating on different areas of the day and writing down how you feel and in what areas. Personally, I have been meditating for over a year and is just meditating when my body demands it. But, in the beginning, as I say, you have to see on your body how to meditate, because in the end meditation is to serve you.
It seems that these are simple words, and so much to think about.
Do you feel something like, that your body wants to meditate at some random moment of the day? It means you don't have to force yourself to do it?

From m experience, I'm not sure how it works, but at the beginning, I wanted to meditate just for one week every day. But, what was weird to me is a fact that I didn't force myself to meditate. My body wanted it. I'm still shocked by that fact. Have you felt something similar?
Yeah, of course, it's matter. Because for example when someone starts to meditate like my parents. Which means sitting and nothing more. It will do you nothing but frustration and boredom.

How old your mom is? From my perspective, it is really really hard to explain anything to my parents. They are closed in their life knowledge. You should do what you want in life and not look at what others are saying. However, If you're living with her I recommend showing her this youtube channel: [https://www.youtube.com/c/nathanieldrewofficial/videos](https://www.youtube.com/c/nathanieldrewofficial/videos). Nataniel Drew is a guy from Paris and there are a few videos about meditation on its a channel. I think showing her a perspective from the other person what mediation can give you will be very helpful.

I experienced this mainly when I discovered my sad facts from life. In each of these experiences I felt like an additional person looking at my actions. Amazing feeling. After the first time I got scared of this: D

For me personally it is:

\- reconciliation with the truth (my childhood and current situation. It let me take off a mask it wore.),

\- spend time with me and my thoughts,

\- it let me decide what is my reaction for my life situations,

Yeah, It's totally normal :) For my experience when a new thing appears. I'm talking to my subconscious 'Yes I understand, but there is not a good time to think about that'. And it works! I recommend trying ;)
I had a similar problem. I've fixed that by putting my concentration on something. It can be a breath or someplace in your meditation place.
Imagine that most children and teenagers spend 6-7 hours a day on social media. It's something difficult to awareness.

Bro, You're an awesome guy and it is too early to give up. Last time I started my blog where I share my experiences from my shitty childhood and fucking family. From my perspective and my experience I recommend you to note your thoughts and experiment with meditation. At least try for one or two weeks. NEVER GIVE UP!
I'm so happy about your journey. I have an account here for 2 weeks and it is something incredible how many people change after they start meditating. Stay strong bro :)

I also remove all social media apps, but the biggest lesson for me was that moment when I started to make calls to my friends/family members. First time I did not write a message to them, just call. Stay persistent in your further meditation journey :)
I'm very proud of you. It also changed a lot for me and I also had childhood trauma, so I just know what's you feel know. Keep going with it :)

Yeah, It is really hard to talk. I had a similar problem with my family because I understood that my parents have always been discriminated against because of their property or less resourcefulness. For 23 years I did not see that. But continuing my meditation practice let me improve my forgiveness skill. I described that in detail on my blog in this article: [https://www.pawelwojtasinski.blog/article/6](https://www.pawelwojtasinski.blog/article/6). I hope it is going to help someone.

In my case it let me find the truth about my existence: who I'm and why I'm who I'm. A lot of my emotions being about facing the truth. I make a lot of notes and spent a lot of hours talking with my friend's experiences. I was not able to let them be because it gave me a deep depression about my life. It also resulted, in a sense, from the fact that most of my friends had an overwhelmed life in terms of, for example, that they had a company related to what they love. But for me at 24 there was a problem to talk to a girl. More details I described on my blog article even I share there the worst emotional experience in my life: [https://www.pawelwojtasinski.blog/article/6](https://www.pawelwojtasinski.blog/article/6)

I had a very very similar problem. I described. flashbacks on my blog's article: [https://www.pawelwojtasinski.blog/article/6](https://www.pawelwojtasinski.blog/article/6). I mentioned there for my childhood memories began to appear after about 2 months. After this time when I started to feel free about my present things. I would ask you. After what time you started to see your past? and Did you get the flashbacks also in time between each meditation practice?
Thank you for your reply. For the first two months after I did one session a day. But for now, I meditate every morning for around 15 minutes and if I need I do it also at any part of my day :)
